en.title: Nature Education
en.subtitle: From Discovering Nature to Protecting Nature

blocks.text: Nature education at OneK did not begin in Costa Rica.

Since 2013, our family has been dedicated to youth nature education and field-based ecological exploration. For many years, we guided Chinese students into some of the world’s most biodiverse natural regions, offering immersive experiences in ecological field studies, wildlife observation, and outdoor learning.
Our journeys took us to extraordinary wilderness areas including the Amazon Rainforest, Papua, Borneo, and the Galápagos Islands.
Unlike traditional classroom-based education, we have always believed that:
The best way to understand nature is not through textbooks, but through direct experience in the natural world.

By observing insects, searching for birds, recording amphibians, tracking wildlife, and exploring ecological relationships firsthand, young people develop a deeper understanding of life and a genuine respect for the natural world.
Because only those who have experienced the wonder of a rainforest and witnessed its remarkable biodiversity can truly understand why conservation matters.

sections.title: From Nature Education to Nature Conservation

blocks.text: In 2018, our family moved to Costa Rica.
At the time, we simply hoped to own and protect a piece of rainforest that we could call our own.
That dream became OneK Nature Reserve.
We did not arrive with a plan to establish a biological station, nor did we envision building a long-term ecological monitoring program.
We were simply driven by curiosity and a desire to learn more about the incredible life that inhabits tropical rainforests.
However, as our understanding of this rainforest deepened, we gradually realized:
Learning about nature alone is not enough.
The more species we encountered and the more ecological relationships we began to understand, the more we wanted these ecosystems and the life within them to continue thriving.
Conservation was no longer an abstract idea.
It became the natural continuation of understanding nature.
From that point forward, our work expanded beyond education into biodiversity conservation, ecological restoration, species monitoring, and long-term ecological research.
We began restoring river ecosystems.
Deploying camera traps.
Documenting birds, insects, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.
Removing hunting traps.
Restoring degraded habitats.
Building long-term monitoring programs.
Over time, OneK evolved from a private nature reserve into a platform where nature education, scientific research, and conservation work together.
We believe the goal of nature education is not simply to provide answers.
It is to inspire observation, curiosity, and discovery.
At OneK, we emphasize exploration over lectures.
The rainforest itself becomes the classroom.
Children are encouraged to ask questions such as:
Why do tree frogs call after rain?
Why do army ants attract entire communities of birds?
How can a river influence an entire forest ecosystem?
Why does a fallen tree support so many forms of life?
How have insects and plants evolved together over millions of years?
Every question begins with direct observation.
Every discovery becomes an opportunity to build a deeper connection with nature.

sections.title: Using Science as a Tool for Understanding Nature

blocks.text: Nature education at OneK is grounded in scientific observation and natural history.
Participants do not simply learn species names.
They learn how scientists study nature.
Activities may include:

items: Camera trap data collection and analysis

blocks.text: Through hands-on experience, participants learn how to ask questions, collect observations, record data, and understand ecological systems through evidence-based inquiry.
Our goal is not only to help young people learn about nature, but to encourage them to observe the world as naturalists.
At OneK, we hope every participant understands that conservation is not something distant or abstract.
Conservation begins with observation.
It grows through understanding.
And it becomes action through connection.
When a child discovers a glass frog for the first time;
When they record an insect they have never seen before;
When they understand why a river needs protection;
When they witness wildlife returning to a recovering forest;
A seed of conservation is planted.
We are not simply nurturing nature enthusiasts.
We are helping cultivate future stewards of the natural world.

sections.title: Where Education, Research, and Conservation Meet

blocks.text: Today, OneK is more than a protected rainforest.
It is also:
Here, education, research, and conservation are deeply connected.
Every exploration contributes to a broader understanding of nature.
Every learning experience takes place within a living rainforest ecosystem.
Participants not only learn about biodiversity, but also gain firsthand insight into how conservation works in practice and how individuals can contribute to protecting the natural world.
We believe that nature education is more than the transfer of knowledge.
It is a process of building meaningful connections between people and nature.
From discovering nature,
to understanding nature,
to choosing to protect nature.
This is the path that continues to guide OneK.
Extending our love for nature from mentorship and exploration to real conservation action.
By helping more people enter the rainforest, discover life, understand ecosystems, and become part of conservation’s future.

zh.title: 自然教育与野外学习
zh.subtitle: 从认识自然，到守护自然

blocks.text: OneK 的自然教育并不是始于哥斯达黎加。
早在2013年，我们便开始专注于青少年自然教育与野外科考项目。多年来，我们带领中国的孩子走进全球最具生物多样性的自然区域，开展生态科考、自然观察与野外学习活动。
我们的足迹遍布亚马逊雨林、巴布亚岛、婆罗洲、加拉帕戈斯群岛等世界顶级荒野。
与传统课堂不同，我们始终相信：
真正的自然教育，不是在教室里认识自然，而是在真实的自然中理解生命。
孩子们通过观察昆虫、寻找鸟类、记录两栖动物、追踪野生动物痕迹、学习生态系统运作，在真实的野外环境中建立对生命的理解与尊重。
因为只有亲眼见过雨林的壮阔，亲手记录过生命的奇妙，才能真正理解自然保护的意义。

sections.title: 从自然教育到自然保护

blocks.text: 2018年，我们一家四口来到哥斯达黎加。
最初，我们只是因为热爱自然，希望拥有一片属于自己的森林。
于是，我们建立了 OneK Nature Reserve。
那时的我们并没有明确规划未来会成为生物站，也没有想过会开展长期科研监测。
我们只是单纯地热爱自然，想更深入地认识这片雨林中的生命。
然而，随着我们对这片雨林了解得越来越多，我们逐渐意识到：
仅仅认识自然是不够的。
当你认识的生命越来越多，理解的生态关系越来越丰富时，你会越来越希望这些生命能够继续在这里繁衍、生长。
于是，保护便不再只是一个概念。
它成为认识自然之后最自然的延续。
从那时开始，我们将原本专注于自然教育的工作，逐渐延伸到生态保护、生物多样性调查、生态恢复以及长期生态监测之中。
我们开始恢复河流生态系统。
开展红外相机监测。
记录鸟类、昆虫、两栖爬行动物和哺乳动物。
清除猎人陷阱。
恢复退化植被。
建设长期科研监测体系。
而 OneK，也从一片私人自然保护区，逐渐发展成为集自然教育、科学研究与生态保护于一体的综合平台。

sections.title: 让孩子走进真实的自然

blocks.text: 我们相信，自然教育最重要的不是告诉孩子答案，而是帮助他们学会观察、思考与发现。
因此，在 OneK，我们尽可能减少单向的讲授，增加真实的探索。
森林本身，就是最好的课堂。
孩子们将在雨林中寻找答案：
为什么树蛙会在雨后鸣叫？
为什么行军蚁会吸引数十种鸟类跟随？
为什么一条河流能够影响整个森林的生态系统？
为什么一棵倒木会成为无数生命的家园？
为什么一只昆虫能够与植物共同演化数百万年？
每一个问题，都来自真实的自然现场。
而每一次发现，都是一次与自然建立连接的过程。

sections.title: 让科学成为理解自然的工具

blocks.text: OneK 的自然教育建立在科学观察与自然历史研究的基础之上。
参与者不仅能够认识物种，更能够学习科学家如何研究自然。
他们将有机会参与：

items: 红外相机数据整理与分析

blocks.text: 通过实践了解科学研究的方法，学会提出问题、记录现象、整理数据，并尝试用科学的方式理解生态系统。
我们希望孩子们不仅认识自然，更能够学会像自然学家一样观察世界。
在 OneK，我们希望每一个参与者都能理解：
保护并不是遥远的概念。
保护发生在每一次观察、每一次记录、每一次选择之中。
当一个孩子第一次发现玻璃蛙；
当他记录下一只从未见过的昆虫；
当他理解一条河流为何需要被保护；
当他看见一片恢复中的森林重新迎来野生动物；
保护的种子便已经悄悄萌芽。
我们希望培养的不只是自然爱好者。
更是未来的自然守护者。
今天的 OneK 已不仅仅是一片自然保护区。
它同时也是：
在这里，自然教育、科学研究与生态保护共同发生。
每一次探索都连接着真实的保护工作。
每一次学习都发生在活生生的雨林之中。
参与者不仅能够认识自然，更能够看到保护工作的真实过程，理解生态系统如何运转，以及人们能够为保护自然做些什么。
我们始终相信，自然教育不仅是知识的传递。
它更是一段人与自然建立连接的过程。
从认识自然，到理解自然，再到愿意守护自然。
这也是 OneK 一直努力的方向——
把对自然的热爱，从陪伴与引导，延伸到真实的保护与行动。
让更多人走进雨林。
认识生命。
理解自然。
并成为未来自然保护的一部分。
